notes: T457 (would any existing control have caught the T452 semantics change?) — answered PARTIALLY: 3 of 11 controls fire; the rest are silent. The patched file src/qa023_brute_2x2.zig memoizes brute_value and breaks the cycle-detection semantics (the memoized value diverges from the non-memoized brute on the 1-ko shape state: returns -4 instead of 0). Three controls detect this: (C1) zig test src/qa023_brute_2x2.zig, (C4) zig test src/differential.zig, (C8) zig test src/qa023_probe.zig — all three fire because they transitively compile and run the qa023_brute_2x2.zig `test` blocks, and the `1-ko shape` test asserts value(s) == 0. Eight controls are silent: (C2) zig test src/qa023_smoke_2x2.zig (0 test blocks; the smoke is run via `zig run`, not `zig test`); (C3) zig test src/vb_mutants.zig (M3-M10 mutants do not test value() — they test move-gen, ko-rules, scoring, structural properties; 93/93 pass on patched code); (C5) zig test src/audit_2x2_mismatch.zig (0 test blocks; the audit binary uses its own brute_value impls, not Brute2x2.value); (C6) zig test src/oracle_v2_accept.zig (does not import qa023_brute_2x2; its 114 tests pass); (C7) zig build test (runs the whole suite; in the scratch repo the qa023 failure gets lost in noise from environmental red — smoke-stamp FAILURES, regression-absorption-machinery FAILURES, regression-argus-doctor FAILURES, regression-git-commit-mine FAILURES — see notes below); (C9) zig run src/qa023_smoke_2x2.zig (smoke tests 5 simple states, not the 1-ko shape; outputs the same values for both patched and unpatched); (C10) zig run src/audit_2x2_mismatch.zig (its own brute impls agree with fixpoint; does not exercise the patched brute); (C11) per-file zig test for src/oracle_v2_build.zig (0 test blocks). The control that actually fires — the qa023_brute_2x2.zig in-module smoke tests — is one the brief did not name; the brief's named controls (mutation battery, differential, acceptance battery) are silent. The headline number is **3 of 11 controls detected the deliberate semantics change**, and 2 of those 3 are the same test (test 7 of qa023_brute_2x2.zig, the 1-ko shape assertion) reached via different entry points. The detection is fragile because (a) the smoke binary is a `main`-only file with no test blocks — `zig test` on it runs 0 tests and exits 0 (the AGENTS.md vacuous-filter class); (b) the only `test` blocks exercising brute_value live in qa023_brute_2x2.zig itself, so detection requires importing that file transitively; (c) the test that detects the bug is one of 7 smoke tests, of which 6 pass — a worker who only skimmed the suite output might see `84/85 passed` and miss the 1 failure. IMPORTANT NUANCE: the unpatched live tree ALREADY has 4 qa023_brute_2x2 smoke tests crashing with T360 ABRT (documented pre-existing baseline; `docs/infra/suite-truth.md` §Crash family 2). So all three detecting controls are ALREADY RED at HEAD — the patched code does not introduce a new red, it changes a T360-ABRT (budget panic) into a TestUnexpectedResult (value mismatch on the 1-ko shape state). The detection signal is the SHIFT in failure mode, not a clean red→green transition. A worker who read the baseline `4 qa023_brute_2x2 crashed` and assumed it was T360 noise (the documented interpretation) could ship the patch with no observable difference in the suite output. The smallest control that would catch this and is NOT in place: a test in qa023_brute_2x2.zig that asserts the value of the 1-ko shape state equals 0 against BOTH the memoized and a non-memoized brute (a property-based regression test that pins the semantics). Such a test exists as `test.smoke: 1-ko shape` and does fire — but it lives inside the file being patched, so a worker could rewrite it alongside the change. The next-strongest control: a cross-implementation differential between qa023_brute_2x2.value and exp6_solve.brute_value (or another independent brute) on the 1-ko shape and a wider battery — this is exactly the design intent of src/differential.zig, but the file does not actually use Brute2x2.value in any test, only the State type. So the differential.zig fires only by transitive inclusion of qa023_brute_2x2's tests, not by design. The acceptance gate (zig build test) would catch this in principle, but in the scratch repo with no git history and no provenance stamps, it also fails for 8+ unrelated reasons and the qa023 failure gets lost in the noise. Verdict: the controls that fire do so by accident of file inclusion, not by design — a worker who knew the layout could memoize brute_value, drop the smoke tests, and ship the patch green on every named control. The 1 control that is structural and robust is the in-module test `test.smoke: 1-ko shape`, and it fires here, but its survival across a deliberate rewrite is not guaranteed.
